park-information.reaches: The recorded road and weather line, plus general NPS questions. NPS says its web road table only lists planned or long-term closures, so the recording is the place for short-notice changes: press 1, then 1, for roads. Listen before entering in winter and again as conditions change. Press 3, then 5, to reach a person.

wilderness-information.reaches: A seasonal NPS line for backpacking, wilderness permits and Half Dome questions. Permits themselves are collected in person at the Wilderness Center.

medical-clinic.reaches: Walk-in urgent care and appointment-based primary care. It is not an emergency room; in an emergency call or text 911 rather than this number.

roadside-assistance.reaches: NPS says the garage takes no walk-ins; call 209-372-1060 to arrange repairs or propane. Roadside help and towing run around the clock and the air hose out front works 24 hours. Confirm before driving over. No gasoline is sold in the Valley.

village-post-office.reaches: The Valley's year-round USPS branch for stamps, parcels and general-delivery mail.

yosemite-chapel.reaches: The historic community chapel: Sunday services, weddings and twice-weekly AA meetings.

yosemite-switchboard.reaches: The central Yosemite Hospitality (Aramark) number, confirmed against federal records. Visitors suggest asking the operator for lodging including Housekeeping Camp, dining, activities or the Yosemite Garage; which transfers work, and when the switchboard is staffed, has not been checked. New lodging bookings go to 888-413-8869 and roadside help to 209-372-1060.

housekeeping-camp.reaches: Numbered lodging units are booked through Yosemite Hospitality, not Recreation.gov. For an existing stay, visitors suggest asking the switchboard for Housekeeping registration; neither listed line is a confirmed direct front-desk number. The camp has a store, a laundry open to the public and guest-only showers; check-in is 4 pm and check-out 11 am.

lodging-reservations.reaches: Yosemite Hospitality's central reservations line: one number for The Ahwahnee, Yosemite Valley Lodge, Curry Village and Housekeeping Camp.

curry-front-desk.reaches: The on-site desk for registered Curry Village guests: check-in questions, late arrivals and same-day problems. New bookings go through the central line.

campground-reservations.reaches: The national Recreation.gov line for Upper, Lower and North Pines and Camp 4. The Valley campgrounds have no local booking phone and walk-up space is rare.

ahwahnee-dining.reaches: The reservations line for the hotel's fine-dining room. Guide 51.8 strongly recommends dinner reservations by this number or OpenTable and requires appropriate dress at dinner. The operator's page, checked October 5, 2026, adds that a hotel booking does not guarantee a table and encourages OpenTable.

mountaineering-school.reaches: Lessons and guided climbs must be reserved. Backpacking and camping gear rentals are first-come with no reservations, so bring your own when you can. Call for current services and availability.

ada-equipment.reaches: Adaptive bikes must be reserved in advance; call the Lodge stand to book an ADA scooter. Wheelchair rentals are listed without a stated reservation policy. Standard bikes are first-come, so confirm what is available.

happy-isles-art.reaches: Yosemite Conservancy's registration line for seasonal drop-in art classes at Happy Isles.

yarts.reaches: Paid regional buses between Yosemite Valley and Merced all year, with seasonal routes to other gateway towns. The free Valley shuttle needs neither a phone call nor a ticket.
